title: Astro Next feature manifest
description: Every Chromium or Astro capability Astro must take a decision about, with that decision.
Validated by tools/policy/manifest.py, which implements this schema directly rather than
importing a validator library: a generator that cannot run until somebody installs a package
is a generator that stops being run. The tool asserts it supports every keyword this file
uses, so an unsupported keyword fails loudly instead of becoming decorative.
TWO STATE FIELDS, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE POINT.
`observed_state` is what the CURRENT legacy build does, evidence-backed and citable.
`state` is the Astro Next DECISION. They are separate fields so that 'an inherited patch
disables this' can never be silently promoted into 'we decided to disable this'. A downstream
issue reading one entry can tell what it inherits from what has been chosen.

states.description: The state vocabulary, defined in this file so a reader never has to guess.

description: What the current legacy build does. `NOT_BUILT` is its own value and not a synonym for
DORMANT: baseline finding 1 measured that nothing links the Astro overlay into the build
graph, so every overlay capability is absent from today's binary through a build defect
(#7) rather than through anybody's decision. Recording that as DORMANT would invent a
decision nobody took.
`DISABLED_BY_BUILD` and `DISABLED_BY_PATCH` are separate for the same reason
DISABLE_BUILD and DISABLE_RUNTIME are: a GN arg switching a component off is a
configuration anybody can read and re-apply, and a patch deleting source lines is not.
Safe Browsing is the entry that makes it concrete -- `safe_browsing_mode = 0` on all six
platform configurations.
`NOT_MEASURED` is the honest value whenever the evidence would amount to 'the epic asked
about it'. Ten entries here carried DISABLED_BY_PATCH on that basis and were corrected:
a listing in a review set is not evidence that anything changed the capability.

id.description: Stable, unique, kebab-case. Code and presubmits reference this.

description: file:line, a patch name, or a named baseline finding. Required with no exception:
an observed state with no evidence is an assertion, and this document exists to stop
assertions being cited as measurements.
Set when the decision is not this manifest's to take. Security-relevant capabilities
-- Safe Browsing, certificate verification, sandboxing, update integrity -- belong to
#20; they are listed here so the matrix is complete and routed so nobody reads the
listing as a decision.
Endpoint ids from the endpoint manifest, or the single literal `none`. Joined
strictly in both directions: an unknown id fails, and an endpoint whose
owning_feature is not declared here fails.
Required whenever state is INVESTIGATE. `question` is the specific thing that is not
known; `answered_by` is the command, experiment or document that settles it. An
INVESTIGATE with no way to leave it is a permanent unknown wearing a temporary label.
Issues whose design depends on THIS entry's decision -- a prerequisite edge. The
named issue cannot state its own design correctly without reading the decision here,
and getting it wrong is a defect in that issue rather than a missing reference.
This is NOT 'the named issue reads this entry'. That relation is `inputs_to`, and the
two were conflated: ten entries declared `blocks: [11]` while carrying already-decided
states, which read as ten pending decisions #11 was waiting on when what #11 actually
needed from them was one column of data. See critical-subset-for-schemes.md.
Issues that READ this entry as reference data. Weaker than `blocks`: the named issue
cites the decision recorded here but does not wait on it, because the decision is
already taken. An entry may not name the same issue in both fields -- one relation or
the other, never both, or the distinction stops meaning anything.

inputs_reason.description: Required with `inputs_to`: exactly what the named issue reads from this entry.

description: The DECIDED bare host name this capability's WebUI data source registers under, or the
literal `not-determined`. Not a restatement of `user_surface`, which records today's
URL: this is the name after #11 removes the astro://-to-chrome:// alias.
It is a manifest field because the WebUI data-source registry is a flat map keyed on
the bare host and shared across every WebUI scheme except chrome-untrusted
(content/browser/webui/url_data_manager_backend.cc:122, :149), and a later same-named
registration silently replaces the earlier one (content/public/browser/url_data_source.cc:52-54).
Two pages that agree on a name are one page, and the loser fails with ERR_INVALID_URL.
Which of Astro's two internal schemes this page lands on. Not a style preference: a
document with WebUI bindings has its network factory revoked
(content/browser/renderer_host/render_frame_host_impl.cc:12645-12657), so a page whose
own JavaScript must reach the network cannot be bound, and therefore cannot be trusted.
`trusted` = astro://, bound, no network factory. `untrusted` = astro-untrusted://,
unbound, keeps one. Declared together with `webui_host`; see webui-scheme-trust-split.
